purpose: Per-section/topic target quotas for building a question BANK/dataset, not a simulation of a single year's paper. Multiply/scale as needed. Mirrors the structure of the JEE Main / GMAT quotas files so banks across exams can be planned/compared side by side.
question_type_note: CLAT UG uses only ONE question format across all five sections: single-correct MCQ attached to a passage/caselet (English, Current Affairs, Legal Reasoning and Logical Reasoning are 100% passage-based; Quantitative Techniques is caselet/data-set based). There is no numerical-value entry, no multiple-correct MCQ, and no standalone fact-recall question anywhere in the current (CLAT 2024 onward) pattern.
difficulty_note: The Consortium does not publish official difficulty tags. Coaching-tracker consensus places CLAT's overall difficulty as moderate, with Legal Reasoning and Quantitative Techniques containing the largest share of harder, multi-step items, and English/Current Affairs skewing easier when the underlying passage is accessible. Tiers below (easy/medium/hard) are seeding targets, not official classifications.

CA.notes: Highest-weightage section along with Legal Reasoning; content decays fast (news-cycle dependent), so a bank needs frequent refresh to stay current for any given test cycle.

LEGAL.notes: Reported by trackers as containing a larger share of harder, multi-step application items than the other passage-based sections.

QUANT.notes: Smallest section by question count, but consistently flagged as disproportionately time-costly relative to its weight because every item requires reading a data caselet first.
